figure_caption: The studied score-space counterfactual changes only selected target coordinates by a common fraction of remaining headroom; all rivals and unselected coordinates stay fixed. Investment counts selected coordinates, not training expense. Mean, conventional median, and symmetric trimmed mean are applied separately to the target and frozen rivals. Median uses the middle value or averages the middle pair; trimming removes floor(m/5) values per tail after re-sorting. Strict first place exceeds the rule-specific best-rival aggregate by epsilon = 10^-10; ties do not win. Failure of full support certifies unattainability by monotonicity. Otherwise, exhaustive search at up to six coordinates and largest-headroom prefixes for larger mean problems certify exact minima. Larger median and trimmed-mean problems yield a verified feasible upper bound combined with an independent lower bound. Support intervals are optimization certificates, not statistical intervals. No model training or quantitative results are represented.

panels.title: Counterfactual investment
panels.short_caption: Only selected target coordinates receive bounded uplift; rivals remain fixed and cost counts coordinates.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: investment is a bounded change to selected target scores with frozen rivals, charged by coordinate count rather than training effort. Build a top-to-bottom schematic with no cross-panel connectors.
Nodes and semantic encoding: matrix (sharp rectangular data region) contains target (a distinctly outlined row of symbolic coordinate tiles labelled x) and rivals (several compact rows grouped as frozen data labelled Frozen rivals). Preserve a separate border around target so only its branch can change. support (small sharp data box, intervention specification, label Support S); ceiling (small sharp data box, intervention specification, label Headroom fraction and standalone $$\alpha$$); uplift (rounded process box, counterfactual operation, label Selected-coordinate uplift); changed (sharp data row, counterfactual output, label Updated target). changed preserves target's coordinate positions. Mark the same subset S in both rows using small selection ticks or a bracket; change only selected tile markers and keep unselected tile markers identical. Tiles have no numerical values. Frozen status uses the rivals' enclosing border and a simple lock glyph; do not draw a transformed rivals region. No trainable components.
formula is an unboxed annotation beside uplift, the ONLY raw multi-term equation in the entire figure: $$x_j^{S,\alpha}=x_j+\alpha(1-x_j)\mathbf{1}\{j\in S\}$$. cost (small outlined definition card, not measured result) has label Coordinate count and standalone $$|S|$$. scope is an unboxed footer labelled Not training cost.
Every edge: target -> uplift solid forward score flow, unlabelled; support -> uplift dashed auxiliary specification, unlabelled; ceiling -> uplift dashed auxiliary specification, unlabelled; uplift -> changed solid forward score flow, unlabelled; support -> cost dashed auxiliary accounting link, unlabelled. No intervention edge touches rivals. There are no training or gradient arrows.
Spatial layout: matrix across the top, target visibly separated from rival rows; support and ceiling flank uplift beneath the matrix; changed aligned below uplift; formula just below the operation or changed row, never in a box; cost and scope form a lower band. Route connectors away from formula. Importance: target-only change and frozen rivals first; support/headroom and coordinate count second; equation third; scope footer last.
Exact text budget excluding title: x; Frozen rivals; Support S; Headroom fraction; alpha as math; Selected-coordinate uplift; Updated target; the single response equation; Coordinate count; |S| as math; Not training cost. No extra prose, numeric examples, palette prescriptions, plots, or placeholders.

panels.title: Aggregation conditions
panels.short_caption: Mean uses every score; conventional median and symmetric trimming depend on the ordering after uplift.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: aggregation rules use different parts of a score vector, and order-statistic rules re-sort after the candidate uplift. This is an independent explanatory schematic with no cross-panel arrows.
Nodes and semantic encoding: vector (sharp data box labelled Score vector); mean (rounded fixed mathematical operation region labelled Mean) contains mean_strip (equal-size score-entry tiles, all included); sort (rounded fixed operation labelled Re-sort after uplift); median (rounded fixed aggregation region labelled Median) contains odd_strip (five ordered abstract tiles, only the middle tile selected, label Odd) and even_strip (six ordered abstract tiles, only the central pair selected, label Even); median_note (unboxed annotation labelled Middle value / pair); trimmed (rounded fixed aggregation region labelled Trimmed mean) contains trim_strip (ten ordered abstract tiles, two per tail visibly crossed out and the six central tiles bracketed together); trim_note (unboxed label Symmetric 20% trimming). mean_out, median_out, trim_out are small unboxed output anchors by their respective regions, labelled with single symbols $$A_{\mathrm{mean}}$$, $$A_{\mathrm{median}}$$, $$A_{\mathrm{trim}}$$. matched is an unboxed scope annotation labelled Rule-matched target / rivals. No operation is trainable; strips are symbolic data, not results.
The median central pair denotes their average, not choosing either value. Use a brace joining that pair to its output edge, with the explanation left to the caption. The floor convention for trimming is in the caption; the ten-tile strip is a valid schematic, not empirical data. Crossed-out tail tiles remain visible. No axes, score values, or quantitative output.
Every edge: vector -> mean solid forward flow, unlabelled; vector -> sort solid forward flow, unlabelled; sort -> median solid forward flow, unlabelled; sort -> trimmed solid forward flow, unlabelled; mean_strip -> mean_out solid aggregation flow, unlabelled; odd_strip -> median_out solid aggregation flow, unlabelled; even_strip's central-pair brace -> median_out solid aggregation flow, unlabelled; trim_strip's retained-center bracket -> trim_out solid aggregation flow, unlabelled. No output flows into another rule or combines the three rules.
Spatial layout: vertically stacked mean, median, trimmed lanes with aligned headings and right output anchors. vector sits above; a left bypass feeds mean while sort feeds only the two lower lanes. Median has two short stacked strips. Place matched at the foot. Importance: selected positions and center-versus-tails first; re-sorting and odd/even median second; rule matching and symbols third.
Exact text budget excluding title: Score vector; Mean; Re-sort after uplift; Median; Odd; Even; Middle value / pair; Trimmed mean; Symmetric 20% trimming; the three aggregate symbols; Rule-matched target / rivals. No equations, extra prose, palette instructions, plotted data, or deferred visuals.

panels.title: Certificate outcomes
panels.short_caption: Full-support screening separates certified impossibility from exact minima and independently bounded support costs.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: monotonic full-support screening and solver regime determine whether the investment certificate is unattainable, exact, or bounded. Draw an independent compact decision flow with no cross-panel connectors.
Nodes and semantic encoding: full (sharp data box, candidate intervention, label Full support); rival (sharp frozen-data box, label Best rival and standalone $$b_r$$); screen (decision diamond, fixed comparator, label Strict-first check); impossible (sharp terminal certificate box, result, label Certified unattainable and standalone $$K_r=\infty$$); route (small routing diamond labelled Panel / rule); enumerate (rounded exact-search process labelled Cardinality enumeration); prefix (rounded exact-mean process labelled Largest-headroom prefix); greedy (rounded feasible-witness process labelled Marginal-gain greedy); exact (sharp terminal certificate box, result, label Exact minimum and standalone $$K_r$$); upper (small sharp verified-witness card, label Feasible upper bound and standalone U); lower (small sharp independent-reference card, label Independent lower bound and standalone L); interval (sharp terminal certificate box, result, label Bounded support and standalone $$[L,U]$$). No component is trainable. Terminal boxes are certificate TYPES, not observed results.
Every edge: full -> screen solid forward candidate evaluation, unlabelled; rival -> screen dashed auxiliary threshold dependency, unlabelled; screen -> impossible solid decision branch labelled Failure; screen -> route solid decision branch labelled Success; route -> enumerate solid routing branch labelled $$m\leq6$$; route -> prefix solid routing branch labelled Large / mean; route -> greedy solid routing branch labelled Large / median, trimmed; enumerate -> exact solid certificate flow, unlabelled; prefix -> exact solid certificate flow, unlabelled; greedy -> upper solid verified-witness flow, unlabelled; upper -> interval solid certificate flow, unlabelled; lower -> interval dashed independent-bound dependency, unlabelled.
Strict-first check means exceeding the rule-specific b_r plus epsilon, never ties; the precise condition belongs in the caption, not another equation. Failed full support is certified by monotonicity, not heuristic exhaustion. Failure branches ONLY from screen, never greedy. Winning full support guarantees feasibility of the finite branch. Large means more than six coordinates.
Spatial layout: full and rival at top, screen beneath; impossible occupies a short side branch before solver routing. Lower region uses three compact stacked solver lanes, enumerate then prefix then greedy. Merge the first two into one exact terminal on the right. Place upper beneath greedy, lower beside upper, both feeding interval at bottom. Orthogonal nonoverlapping connectors and legible edge labels; preserve a visibly distinct unattainable branch and two finite certificate endpoints. Importance: three outcome types first; full-support failure versus finite search second; solver regimes and independent lower bound third.
Exact text budget excluding title: Full support; Best rival; b_r as math; Strict-first check; Certified unattainable; K_r=infinity as math; Panel / rule; Failure; Success; m<=6 as math; Large / mean; Large / median, trimmed; Cardinality enumeration; Largest-headroom prefix; Marginal-gain greedy; Exact minimum; K_r as math; Feasible upper bound; U; Independent lower bound; L; Bounded support; [L,U] as math. No multi-term equations, numeric performance results, statistical error bars, palette prescriptions, or placeholders.
